title: Binary Tree Right Side View
statement: Given the root of a binary tree, imagine yourself standing on the right side of it, return the values of the nodes you can see ordered from top to bottom.
inputFormat: A single line containing space-separated strings mapping the level-order traversal of the tree (`null` for empty nodes).
outputFormat: Space-separated integers: the right side view from top to bottom.
constraints:
0 <= The number of nodes in the tree <= 100
-100 <= Node.val <= 100

examples.explanation: Looking from right, we see root 1, node 3 on level 1, and node 4 on level 2.

starterCode.python:
import sys
line = sys.stdin.read().split()
# Implement BFS/DFS taking the last node of each level
